title: Vinted Blamed You for "Insufficient Packaging"? What It Means and How to Fight It (UK)
intro: If Vinted rules that an item arrived damaged because of "insufficient packaging", the buyer gets a full refund through Buyer Protection — and sellers report that the buyer keeps the item, you get no payout, and there is no carrier compensation to fall back on. The verdict is one of the most complained-about outcomes on r/vinted, r/vintedUK and the big Facebook seller groups, and it is usually delivered as a final, non-negotiable decision. This guide explains what "insufficient packaging" actually means, why so many sellers are losing these cases, and the steps that give you any real chance of fighting it.
meta_description: Vinted ruled your parcel arrived damaged because of "insufficient packaging"? What the verdict means, why sellers keep losing these cases, how to appeal, and how to pack so you never get hit again.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Get ahead of the scammers — get alerted the moment items are listed

body.heading: What "insufficient packaging" actually means on Vinted
paragraphs: Vinted's help article "Package was damaged in transit" (help article 729) sets out the buyer's side of the process: within 2 days of the delivery notification, the buyer reports the issue and submits photos of the damage, photos of the packaging from every side (inside and out), the tracking number, and a photo of the shipping label. If Vinted confirms the item was damaged during shipping, the order is cancelled and the buyer is fully refunded under Buyer Protection. Investigations and refunds can take up to several weeks.

The "insufficient packaging" verdict is what happens when Vinted decides the damage wasn't the carrier's fault — it was the way you packed it. In that scenario, the refund still goes to the buyer, but the loss lands on you: sellers who have been through it report getting no compensation and no way to claim from the carrier, because Vinted has classified the cause as your packaging rather than the shipping process.

Sellers describe the pattern in near-identical terms across Reddit and Facebook: a buyer reports "arrived damaged", the order is suspended, and the response comes back blaming the packaging. One r/vinted seller who had photographed the entire packing process reported that Vinted "didn't care" about the proof and refunded the buyer anyway. Another was told the damage was "caused by insufficient packaging" and that they were "not eligible for compensation" — after appealing.

body.heading: Why sellers keep losing these cases
paragraphs: The first problem is the claim route. When a buyer selects "damaged in transit", the case goes straight to Vinted rather than back to you for negotiation. That matters: with a "not as described" claim you get options — a partial refund, a full refund, or asking for the item back. With a damage claim, sellers report there is no such menu — Vinted investigates and decides, and the seller is mostly a spectator.

The second problem is that buyers have caught on. On these threads, commenters repeatedly point out that a damage claim is an easy way to get a refund while keeping the item, because when the damage is ruled a packaging problem the item is not returned. Sellers describe being hit more than once: one seller in a Facebook group said they had been accused of "insufficient packaging" five separate times.

The third problem is the appeal wall. Sellers who fight the verdict describe the same experience: automated replies, a "our review is final" message, and support that won't look again even with new evidence. One r/vintedUK seller who contested a claim for over a month never got past the final-decision message, despite hundreds of five-star reviews and photos of the packaging they had used.

body.heading: What to do if you've been hit with the verdict
paragraphs: First, don't reply to the automated message expecting a human. Reply inside the original order or issue thread with everything in one place: photos of the item before shipping, the packaging at every stage, the sealed parcel with the label visible, the drop-off receipt, and any carrier delivery photo showing the parcel arrived intact. Support can see the full thread history, so one consolidated, factual reply is far stronger than scattered messages.

Then escalate through the help centre. Open any help article roughly related to the problem and use the "Contact us" / "I still need help" button at the bottom of the page — that opens the support form without needing a new order attached. For issues the normal form can't resolve, Vinted lists a legal contact for legal and regulatory matters, though sellers report replies there are slow and often still final.

Be realistic about the odds. Across the threads, sellers who got a decision reversed are rare; the realistic goals are (a) getting the case re-reviewed with full evidence on record, and (b) if the damage genuinely happened in transit, pushing Vinted to treat it as a shipping claim rather than a packaging failure. Keep the tone factual, attach everything, and stay in one thread.

body.heading: How to protect yourself before you ship
paragraphs: The verdict is decided on photos, and most sellers who lose admit they had no evidence of how the item was packed. The fix takes two minutes: photograph or film the item, then the item inside its protection, then the sealed parcel with the label visible, then the drop-off receipt, and keep the tracking number. If a dispute ever happens, that's your entire defence in one folder.

Pack so the parcel survives, not just so it looks tidy. Anything fragile or valuable should go in a rigid box or padded mailer with bubble wrap or crumpled paper as void-fill. Books in flimsy cardboard sleeves are the most common packaging complaint in these threads: several sellers lost book claims because the buyer photographed a soft envelope and Vinted agreed it was inadequate.

Match the packaging to the item's value. A poly mailer is fine for a t-shirt; a £50 book, glass, ceramics, or anything breakable should be packed as if the courier will throw it — because statistically, it will be thrown at least once. When the packaging clearly matches the item, a damage claim becomes much harder for a buyer to win.

body.heading: The pattern to be aware of
paragraphs: This isn't a one-off horror story — it's a recognised pattern. The same shape appears again and again: buyer reports damage, Vinted investigates, packaging is blamed, buyer is refunded and keeps the item, seller is left with nothing. Some are genuine courier damage where Vinted's verdict is simply harsh; some are buyers exploiting the system; and sellers can't tell which is which from the automated reply.

The defence is the same either way: pack properly, document everything, and if you're hit, reply in-thread with your evidence and escalate through the help centre. You can't control Vinted's decision — but you can control whether you walk into the dispute empty-handed.

faq.question: What does "insufficient packaging" mean on Vinted?
faq.answer: It's Vinted's term for packaging it judges not robust enough to protect the item during normal courier handling. When damage is blamed on it, the buyer is refunded under Buyer Protection and the seller is not compensated, because the cause is classified as the seller's packaging rather than the shipping process.

faq.question: If Vinted rules insufficient packaging, does the buyer have to return the item?
faq.answer: Sellers report that no return is required: the buyer keeps the item and gets a full refund, and the loss lands on the seller. Vinted's damaged-in-transit help article says the order is cancelled and the buyer fully refunded once damage is confirmed — the return question only arises with "not as described" claims.

faq.question: Can I appeal an "insufficient packaging" decision?
faq.answer: You can try. Reply inside the original issue thread with all your evidence — packaging photos, drop-off receipt, delivery photo — and escalate via the "Contact us" button at the bottom of a help centre article. Be aware that sellers report reversals are rare and that responses often come back as automated "our review is final" messages.

faq.question: How long does a damaged-in-transit case take?
faq.answer: Vinted's official help article says damaged package investigations and refunds can take up to several weeks. The buyer has 2 days from the delivery notification to report the issue, after which the order is suspended while Vinted investigates.

faq.question: Does the seller ever get compensated when a parcel is damaged?
faq.answer: Yes, in principle — when the packaging is judged adequate, the damage is treated as a shipping issue and the seller should be covered. But sellers report Vinted frequently concludes the packaging was at fault instead, which is exactly why photographic evidence of your packing process is the single most valuable thing you can keep.

faq.question: What should I photograph before shipping a Vinted order?
faq.answer: Four things: the item itself, the item inside its packaging, the sealed parcel with the shipping label clearly visible, and the drop-off receipt. Also screenshot the tracking once it's collected. Keep them together until the buyer confirms everything is OK.
